newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - trade.

text.p: Midwest cash hog prices early Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by an increase in hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota actual hog marketings Monday came in at 110,000 head, above the estimate for 105,000, USDA said. Tuesday's estimate was 105,000 head.

Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to plants were expected to range from $53.50 to $54.00. Illinois tops were seen at $54.00 to $54.50 at the plant and Indiana top prices at plants were seen at $52.50.
Packer demand has remained strong on gains in wholesale pork prices which kept operating margins profitable, market sources said.
The strong demand, along with increased marketings, could result in a large Saturday slaughter and possible weekly kill of 1.9 million head, the largest since mid-May, said one Iowa hog buyer.
"It all depends on what people want to do on Saturday," the buyer said.
